To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the rTg 4510 model is a useful tool to investigate tau pathology and that the model is suitable for the evaluation of therapeutic strategies.

pathological tau in rTG4510 mice carries multiple post-translatioanl modifications that accumulate in a steady age-dependent fashion and that total tau in CSFTau in CSF is a promising biomarker of tau pathology.

the rTg 4510 mouse model develops tau pathology that is accompanied by the accumulation of a complex pool of pathological tau carrying multiple post-translatory modifications, a process which can be detected well-before the histological detection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and characterization of the rT4510 model and its application in the search for tau-based therapies.
the development of tau pathology in a mouse model and its implications in translational research.

the development of a comprehensive panel of tau immunoassays that can be used to characterize the pathological tau pool in rTg 4510 mice and to better enable drug discovery efforts targeting pathological tau.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rTg 4510 model is a valuable model for tau pathology and can be used to develop therapeutic strategies for tauopathy.
the rTg 4510 mice are a good model for studying tau pathology, but not a good model for the study of tau pathology and CSF tau as biomarker.
the rTg 4510 mouse model is suitable for drug discovery efforts aimed at reducing tau pathology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rTg45 10 mouse model provides a unique tool for studying tau pathology in vivo.

tauopathies in rTg 4510 mice are associated with the accumulation of a heterogeneous pool of post-translationally-modified tau that can be detected by immunoassays in brain homogenates well before histological detection of tau pathology.

The main takeaway from our work is that
CSF tau is a very dynamic molecule that changes in a multiphasic manner across the lifespan.
the use of the rTgs4510 mouse as a translational model for tauopathies should be done with the knowledge that there are important differences between this mouse model and the human condition.
CSF tau is not a static measure of disease progression but a highly dynamic biomarker that requires careful interpretation.
